match_note: Figures and claims match v1: v1 cites 'Figure 1d' for Shapiro steps and a nonexistent 'Figure 1e', contains 'Our experiments confirm' and 'unequivocal evidence', the Sigrist and Agterberg statement, Ring 1/Ring 2 diode data, and no Yerin et al. citations, all as the round-1 reports describe. One difference: the reviewed manuscript was titled 'Inherent Josephson diodes in a multi-component order parameter superconductor' (quoted by R2), while arXiv v1 is titled 'Time-reversal symmetry breaking in microscopic single-crystal Sr2RuO4 devices'. The file covers only Communications Physics versions (transferred from another journal). Rounds: v0 R1-R3; v1 R1 minor, R2 accept, R3 still not convinced; v2 R1 and R3 accept with wording changes. L4 and L5 concern the revised toy-model text and the Delta I_TRSB quantity introduced in revision.

concerns.quote: it is difficult to understand the main message of the authors of this manuscript. Do they want to prove that there is a TRSB state in this superconductor?
concerns.summary: The main message is unclear: is the paper about proving TRSB or about a Josephson diode effect?

concerns.quote: The authors should provide a clearer and more precise definition of a domain wall.
concerns.summary: Define what a domain wall is in a multicomponent order parameter (phase soliton or modulus kink) and its role in the interpretation.

concerns.quote: the theoretical justifications for the diode effect by means of a certain domain wall do not seem convincing.
concerns.summary: Diode effects occur in conventional/multicomponent junctions without any domain walls, so the domain-wall explanation is unconvincing and relevant work is ignored.

concerns.quote: Why don't the authors show the full CVC at the beginning of the article, starting from negative current values, to see its asymmetry?
concerns.summary: Only a narrow positive-bias section of the I-V curve is shown; the full curve for both polarities is needed to see asymmetry.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: what the dimensions of the rings are and how these dimensions relate to the London penetration depth and coherence length
concerns.summary: Ring dimensions and their relation to penetration depth and coherence length should be in the main text.

concerns.quote: it is logical to expect a figure in the main text of the article showing the dependence of the rectification coefficient on the applied magnetic field and temperature.
concerns.summary: A diode paper should show the rectification coefficient versus field and temperature.

concerns.quote: What type of Josephson weak coupling do the authors mean? Is it a tunnel contact or a constriction-type contact?
concerns.summary: The nature of the Josephson weak link is unspecified.

concerns.quote: the occurrence of \varphi_0 and \varphi Josephson contacts was also shown in the following works
concerns.summary: Prior work on phi0 and phi junctions between conventional and multicomponent superconductors is not cited.

concerns.quote: Figure 1d is not discussed at all in the text.
concerns.summary: Figure panel references are wrong: the text cites Fig. 1d for Shapiro steps shown in Fig. 1c, Fig. 1d is not discussed, and a nonexistent Fig. 1e is cited.

concerns.quote: This can be misleading as it gives the reader the impression that chiral domain walls are pinned by defects/notches created in the middle of the ring
concerns.summary: Schematics show notches pinning the domain walls that do not exist in the real devices.

concerns.quote: The authors should perform this control experiment in order to make their claim that the observed effects are induced by the presence of chiral superconducting domain walls more robust.
concerns.summary: Drive the ring into a monodomain state (high field, field cooling, or a geometry without walls) and show that the effects vanish.

concerns.quote: Can the sign of the diode effect be reversed with thermal cycling? Have the authors observed this?
concerns.summary: The diode sign is nearly always negative; test reversal by thermal cycling and explain what selects one domain arrangement over a degenerate one.

concerns.quote: There is a certain periodicity of the diode effect at higher temperatures (1000 mK), which then turns almost constant at intermediate temperatures(400 mK) and appears irregular at lower temperatures (50 mK).
concerns.summary: The temperature-dependent field pattern of the diode effect is unexplained by the model.

concerns.quote: The zero-field diode effect is strong at high temperatures (Fig.2c), whereas it looks to be almost zero at 50 mK (Fig. 2b).
concerns.summary: The zero-field diode effect being weakest at lowest temperature is counterintuitive and needs explanation.

concerns.quote: These discrepancies in symmetry are quite unusual for an effect claimed to be "inherent".
concerns.summary: The field symmetry of the diode polarity differs between Ring 1 and Ring 2, which is odd for an intrinsic effect.

concerns.quote: Could the authors clarify how they distinguish a truly intrinsic zero-field SDE from an extrinsic one caused by a small residual H offset?
concerns.summary: A residual field or trapped flux could produce an apparent zero-field diode effect; the remnant-field cancellation is unclear.

concerns.quote: the manuscript lacks discussion regarding the physical origin of this phenomenon.
concerns.summary: The mechanism of the bias-current-switchable bistable critical current is not discussed.

concerns.quote: the conclusions are stated with a degree of certainty that may not be fully justified given the complexity of the material system.
concerns.summary: The tone is over-assertive ('Our experiments confirm', 'unequivocal evidence') and the title's 'Inherent' and 'multi-component order parameter' are too bold.

later_concerns.quote: statements implying that the manuscript definitively “establishes” superconducting domain walls or the microscopic order-parameter structure should be replaced by more cautious wording
later_concerns.summary: Soften claims that domain walls are established; they are inferred, not imaged.

later_concerns.quote: the authors should more clearly separate direct experimental facts from model-dependent interpretation.
later_concerns.summary: Separate observations from the domain-wall interpretation.

later_concerns.quote: it should not be presented as a unique fingerprint of domain-wall displacement by itself.
later_concerns.summary: Non-Phi0 SQUID periodicity can arise in multiband Josephson interferometers without domain-wall motion; cite prior work or soften.

later_concerns.quote: the manuscript should make clearer that this toy model does not describe the microscopic spatial structure of the domain wall.
later_concerns.summary: State that the sigmoid domain-wall toy model is phenomenological, not a microscopic solution.

later_concerns.quote: it would be useful to define the conventional zero-field diode efficiency η
later_concerns.summary: Define the diode efficiency eta or explain the focus on Delta I_TRSB.

later_concerns.quote: representative full-range current-voltage characteristics for both current polarities would be useful, at least in the Supplementary Information.
later_concerns.summary: Add full-range I-V curves for both polarities.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: the authors should carefully correct remaining typographical and grammatical issues
Such extrinsic artifacts cannot be unambiguously ruled out by the present data.
later_concerns.summary: A residual field or trapped flux could mimic the zero-field diode effect; systematic thermal and field-modulation measurements are needed.

later_concerns.quote: It appears from Fig. 2 that ΔI_c = I_c+(H)-I_c-(H) follows even symmetry in field, which does not uniquely point to TRSB.
later_concerns.summary: Overlaying Ic+(H) and Ic-(-H) adds no independent TRSB evidence; even-in-field asymmetry can come from polar structure as in Ali et al.

later_concerns.quote: I still think that the phrase “universal Φ0 periodicity of SQUIDs” should be formulated more carefully.
later_concerns.summary: Qualify the 'universal Phi0 periodicity' wording and mention multiband precedents (round 3).

later_concerns.quote: I also recommend that the authors replace overly assertive terms such as “demonstrate”, “establish”, and “provide microscopic evidence” with softer wording.
later_concerns.summary: Final round: soften remaining assertive wording.
